doc.title: Etta Jones interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 2, 1998

chapter: Songs, singers and the state of jazz
title: Dancing to the big bands and the Savoy
summary: She remembers dancing to Basie, Lunceford and Kenton and sneaking into the Savoy to hear Lucky Millinder and the Savoy Sultans.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands

blocks.x: No, no, no, please don’t. Houston was talking about how he’d love to see people dancing again.
I do too. See when I came up we were dancing to Count Basie and Jimmy Lunceford and Andy Kirk.
Yeah, and I think the musicians got off on that too.

And Benny Goodman and Stan Kenton. We’d go down to the Paramount downtown to see Stan Kenton. And I mean we almost wanted to get up in the aisles and sometimes they would do that, get up in the aisles. But now—
What about The Savoy. Did you ever get to the Savoy?
Oh yeah. I went to the Savoy all the time. I used to put my age up and go. One time my girlfriend and I went and she said a date and I said another date and he said “get out of

here” he wouldn’t let us. He said, “Where were you born,” and, “where were you born?” She said 19— He said, “Go.” But we used to go. After a while they got so they knew us and they would let us in so I’d see all of them, Lucky Millinder, all the bands there.
And did they have the two bands sometimes?
Two bands. The Savoy Sultans would be there, and the main band that was really nice.
Yeah. It was continuous music, and continuous dancing. It was wonderful.
